description.narrative: The proposed Second Disaster Resilience Improvement Program will support the government in strengthening its policies and institutional frameworks on DRRM, including disaster response, at national and subnational levels. In so doing, it will help the Philippines adopt an anticipatory approach to disaster response and achieve long-term resilience by addressing underlying sources of risks in its systems.

Reform area: Disaster risk financing enhanced
Outcome: By 2030, at least eight cities have enhanced their disaster risk financing sources by signing parametric insurance policies with GSIS. (2023 Baseline: 0)
Description: 1.6. To provide an additional source of disaster risk financing and support quicker economic recovery, the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) launched its voluntary city-level parametric disaster insurance scheme, commissioned comprehensive catastrophe risk models specific to target cities (including client engagement and portfolio modelling tools and a post-event loss calculation methodology), and built the capacity of GSIS and city government officials in 18 cities. (GSIS)

Reform area: National, provincial and city-level DRRM planning processes harmonized
Outcome: a. By 2030, GEDSI-responsive Local DRRM Plans of at least 20% of provinces (or 17 provinces) and at least 6% of cities or municipalities (or 100 cities or municipalities) are aligned with higher level plans, in accordance with the government's updated national policies on DRRM plans. (2023 Baseline: 0)
Description: 1.1. To improve effectiveness and efficiency in the allocation and transfer of DRRM-related national funds, the government issued a PFM reform roadmap that includes the strengthening of DRRM-related national budget systems, and approved the adoption of a DRRM-related diagnostic tool and the Climate Responsive Public Financial Management Framework in its Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability (PEFA) assessment. (DBM)

Reform area: Performance of GOCCs in disaster response improved
Outcome: By 2030, at least 60% of completed disaster-related PAPs containing GEDSI related targets, from 2025 to 2029, have successfully achieved such targets. (2023 Baseline: 0)
Description: 1.4. To improve the performance of GOCCs on disaster-related programs, activities and projects (PAPs), the government will issue an enhanced Corporate Governance and Performance Scorecard for GOCCs, which will include disaster-related and GEDSI indicators, such as an increase in the representation of women and other vulnerable groups in senior management and governing boards of GOCCs, and increase in the utilization of gender budget of GOCCs to finance GEDSI PAPs related to DRRM. (GCG and DOF-PCAG)
